description_ru: Двое бывших одноклассников случайно встречаются в поезде: один ещё не написал речь для свадьбы сестры, другая едет на собеседование.
text:
Dee: Excuse me, is this seat free? ... Wait a moment. Nick? Nick Ward?
Nick: Yes? Do I know... Dee? Dee Parker? No way!
Dee: Ten years! Look at you. You've got a beard.
Nick: And you've got short hair. You had a long plait at school. I used to pull it.
Dee: I remember. I hit you with a geography book.
Nick: And I cried. I told the teacher I was bleeding, and I wasn't.
Dee: Ha! Move your bag. I'm sitting here.

Nick: What a coincidence. Where are you going?
Dee: To Leeds, for a job interview. I'm very nervous. Look at my hands.
Nick: They're shaking. What's the job?
Dee: Teaching assistant in a primary school. I finished my course in the summer. And you? Are you going to Leeds too?
Nick: I'm going to my sister's wedding. Next to Leeds, in a small village. I'm the best man, and I'm terrified.
Dee: Why?
Nick: Because I have to give a speech, and I haven't written a single word. I've got the ring in my pocket. But no speech.
Dee: How long is the journey?
Nick: Two hours and ten minutes. So I've got just enough time to panic.

Dee: Show me. What have you got so far?
Nick: Nothing. Look. Just the first line, "Ladies and gentlemen." I've crossed it out three times.
Dee: Why?
Nick: It sounds too serious. Like I'm going to read the news.
Dee: Then try something funnier. Tell a story about your sister. What's she like?
Nick: Well. She's called Bea. She's smart, she's stubborn, and she can't cook. Once she tried to make pancakes for my birthday and set fire to a tea towel.
Dee: Perfect. Use that.
Nick: I can't say that at her wedding. Her husband's mother will be there.
Dee: Then say something she can't be angry about. Something true and kind.

Nick: Let me think. When I was fifteen, I lost my keys at night in the rain. I called Bea, and she came on her bicycle. She stayed outside with me for two hours until our parents came home.
Dee: That's lovely. Write it down.
Nick: I don't have a pen. Wait. Do you?
Dee: I've got a pencil and the back of my interview papers. Be quick. I'll need them in an hour.
Nick: This is the best day of my life. A pencil! Okay. "When I was fifteen..."
Dee: Don't read it aloud yet. Write the whole thing first. Then read it.
Nick: Yes, teacher.
Dee: Not yet. But soon, I hope.

Nick: Done! Listen: "When I was fifteen, I lost my keys. My sister came on her bicycle and sat with me in the rain. She's the kind of person who stays. Bea, I'm so happy that Tom has found someone who stays." What do you think?
Dee: Nick, it's good. It's really good. I've got goose bumps.
Nick: Really? You aren't just being nice?
Dee: I was never nice to you at school. Remember the geography book.
Nick: True. So it must be good.
Dee: Now, will you help me, too? I need to practise my answers.
Nick: Of course. I'll be the strict headteacher. Ask me anything.

Dee: No, you ask me. You're the headteacher. Pretend I'm sitting in your office.
Nick: Ahem. Miss Parker. Why do you want to work with children?
Dee: Because children say what they think. And because they make me laugh. Also, I was a terrible pupil, and I want to help the next one who's like me.
Nick: Interesting. Were you really terrible?
Dee: I hit a boy with a book once.
Nick: That's not what you're supposed to say in an interview!
Dee: It's honest. Isn't honesty good?
Nick: Honesty is good. Violence against headteachers is not.

Dee: Okay, a serious question. What if they ask about my weakness?
Nick: Say you work too hard. Everybody says that.
Dee: I don't work too hard. I'm always late. I'm even late for my own birthday.
Nick: Then say you're improving. Your weakness is that you've been late, but you now arrive early. As you did today.
Dee: I arrived at the station twenty minutes early. Because I was so nervous.
Nick: There you go. A story with a happy ending.
Dee: Thank you. You're a better headteacher than anybody I met at school.

Announcer: We're now approaching Leeds. Please take all your belongings with you.
Dee: Already? That was fast.
Nick: Two hours and ten minutes. I wrote a speech and you passed an interview before lunch.
Dee: I haven't passed it yet. But I feel ready.
Nick: Give me your number. We shouldn't wait another ten years.
Dee: Only if you invite me to the wedding.
Nick: Invite you? Bea will love you. You've got the same hair now.
Dee: Hmm. I'll take that as a compliment. Good luck, Nick. And don't lose the ring.
Nick: Don't remind me. Where's my pocket? ... Oh, here it is.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Долгий звук между «э» и «ё», губы расслаблены; не произносите «р» в британском варианте.
Долгий «и», губы растянуты в улыбку; не сокращайте звук.
Кончик языка слегка между зубами, воздух выдыхайте мягко; не заменяйте на «с» или «з».
Задняя часть языка касается нёба, воздух идёт через нос; не добавляйте «г» в конце.

questions.question: Where is Dee going and why?
questions.answer: To Leeds, for a job interview.

questions.question: Why is Nick worried?
questions.answer: He must give a speech at his sister's wedding and has not written it.

questions.question: What story does Nick use in his speech?
questions.answer: His sister came on her bicycle and stayed with him in the rain.

questions.question: What does Dee say she did to Nick at school?
questions.answer: She hit him with a geography book.
